title: Admin - Display Admin Permissions - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Display Admin Permissions feature on the Y4J platform. This feature displays permissions as tags under each admin card, reflecting the latest permission settings. The edge case of UI overflow when too many permissions are assigned must also be handled accessibly. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for semantic structure, screen reader compatibility, visual requirements (contrast, color independence), and responsive/overflow behavior.

testCases.title: Permission tags have a descriptive group label
testCases.componentElement: Permission tags group under admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Internal Administrators page is loaded with at least one admin card that has permissions assigned
steps: Navigate to an admin card's permission tags section using screen reader
Verify the tags group has a descriptive label (e.g., 'Permissions' or 'Assigned Permissions')
Verify the label is programmatically associated (via aria-label, aria-labelledby, or heading)
Verify screen reader announces the group context before reading individual tags
expectedResults: Permission tags section has an accessible group label
Screen reader announces the label (e.g., 'Assigned Permissions') before listing tags
Label is programmatically associated with the tags container
Users understand the tags represent permissions for that specific admin
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand the context of the permission tags

testCases.title: Permission tags use semantic list structure
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with multiple permission tags is displayed
steps: Inspect the permission tags container using developer tools or screen reader
Verify tags are wrapped in a semantic list (ul/ol with li) or have role='list' with role='listitem'
Navigate through the tags with screen reader
Verify screen reader announces the number of items in the list
expectedResults: Permission tags use semantic list markup or ARIA list roles
Screen reader announces 'list with X items' when entering the tags section
Each tag is a list item
Users can understand how many permissions are assigned
testCases.postconditions: Tags are semantically structured for assistive technologies

testCases.title: Each permission tag has readable accessible text
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Navigate to each permission tag using screen reader
Verify each tag announces its permission name (e.g., 'User Management', 'Analytics')
Verify no tag is empty or announces only a generic role without text
Verify tags are not announced as interactive elements unless they are clickable
expectedResults: Each tag announces its full permission name
Screen reader reads: 'User Management', 'Vendor Management', 'Product Approval', etc.
Tags are announced as static text (not buttons/links) unless they have interactive behavior
No empty or unlabeled tags exist
testCases.postconditions: All permission tags are readable by screen readers

testCases.title: Permission tag text has sufficient color contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Use a contrast checker tool (e.g., axe DevTools, Colour Contrast Analyser)
Measure the contrast of tag text against the tag background color
Measure the contrast of the tag background against the admin card background
Check all different permission tags (they may have different colors)
expectedResults: Tag text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against tag background
Tag as a UI component has at least 3:1 contrast against the card background
All permission tags meet contrast requirements regardless of their color scheme
Text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: All permission tags are visually accessible

testCases.title: Permission tags do not rely on color alone to convey meaning
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Observe the permission tags visually
Check if different permissions use different colors
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify each permission is still identifiable by its text label alone
expectedResults: Each permission tag has a text label that identifies it (not relying on color coding alone)
In grayscale mode, all permissions are still identifiable by their text
If color coding is used, it is supplementary to the text label
No information is lost when color is removed
testCases.postconditions: Permission information is accessible regardless of color perception

testCases.title: Permission tags reflect latest settings (dynamic update is accessible)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card is displayed, permissions have just been updated
steps: Edit an admin's permissions (add or remove a permission)
Save the changes
Navigate back to the admin card
Verify the permission tags are updated to reflect the latest settings
Verify screen reader can read the updated tags
If update happens dynamically (without page reload), verify aria-live announces the change
expectedResults: Permission tags immediately reflect the latest saved permissions
Screen reader can read the updated tag values
If dynamic update: change is announced via aria-live='polite' or the user is informed
No stale/cached permission data is displayed
testCases.postconditions: Permission tags always show current data accessibly

testCases.title: UI overflow with many permissions is handled accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, an admin has all 8 permissions assigned (maximum tags)
steps: View an admin card with all permissions assigned
Observe how the tags handle overflow (wrapping, truncation, or 'show more')
If tags wrap: verify all are visible and readable
If truncated with 'show more': verify the trigger is keyboard accessible and has accessible name
If scrollable: verify scroll area is keyboard accessible
expectedResults: All permissions are accessible (either visible or reachable via accessible mechanism)
If wrapping: tags wrap to multiple lines without clipping text
If 'show more' pattern: button has accessible name (e.g., 'Show 3 more permissions'), is keyboard accessible
If scrollable: scroll area is keyboard navigable
No permission information is permanently hidden from assistive technology users
testCases.postconditions: All permissions are accessible even when many are assigned

testCases.title: Overflow 'show more' button (if present) is keyboard and screen reader accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card has overflow with a 'show more' mechanism
steps: Tab to the 'show more' button/link (if overflow pattern is used)
Verify it receives visible focus
Verify screen reader announces its name and role (e.g., '+3 more, button')
Press Enter or Space to expand/show hidden permissions
Verify all hidden permissions become visible and readable
Verify screen reader can access the newly revealed permissions
expectedResults: 'Show more' control is reachable via Tab
Visible focus indicator appears
Screen reader announces descriptive name (e.g., 'Show 3 more permissions, button')
Enter/Space reveals hidden permissions
Revealed permissions are accessible to screen reader
If expanded state: aria-expanded='true' is set

testCases.title: Permission tags are readable at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify all permission tags are still visible
Verify tag text is not clipped or truncated
Verify tags wrap appropriately without horizontal scrolling
Verify overflow mechanism (if any) still works
expectedResults: All tag text is fully readable at 200% zoom
Tags wrap to multiple lines if needed (no horizontal overflow)
No text is clipped or hidden
Overflow mechanism (if present) remains functional
No horizontal scrollbar appears for tag content
testCases.postconditions: Permission tags are fully readable at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Permission tags reflow at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify permission tags reflow without horizontal scrolling
Verify all tag text is readable
Verify tags do not overlap each other or other card content
expectedResults: Tags reflow to fit narrow viewport (stack vertically or wrap)
No horizontal scrollbar for tag content
All tag text remains readable
No overlap between tags or with other card elements
testCases.postconditions: Permission tags work on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Permission tags are within the admin card's semantic structure
testCases.componentElement: Permission tags position in card structure
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin cards with permission tags are displayed
steps: Navigate through an admin card using screen reader
Verify permission tags are read as part of the admin card content
Verify tags appear after the admin's basic info (name, email, role, status)
Verify the reading order is logical: admin info → permissions
expectedResults: Permission tags are semantically within the admin card container
Screen reader reads tags as part of the card's content flow
Reading order is logical (admin details first, then permissions)
Tags are not orphaned or disconnected from their admin card
testCases.postconditions: Tags are properly associated with their admin card

testCases.title: Permission tags content order is meaningful without CSS
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Disable CSS in the browser
Verify permission tags are still presented in a meaningful order
Verify the group label appears before the individual tags
Verify tags are readable in sequence
expectedResults: Without CSS, tags appear in a logical reading order
Group label (e.g., 'Permissions:') appears before the tag list
Individual tags are listed sequentially
No information is lost or reordered confusingly
testCases.postconditions: Content sequence is meaningful regardless of styling

testCases.title: Empty permissions state is communicated accessibly
testCases.componentElement: Admin card with no permissions (if applicable)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, an admin card exists where permissions section might be empty (e.g., Super Admin role with implicit full access)
steps: Navigate to an admin card that may not display permission tags
If no tags are shown, verify the absence is communicated (e.g., 'All permissions' for Super Admin, or 'No specific permissions assigned')
Verify screen reader does not encounter an empty unlabeled container
expectedResults: If no tags are displayed, the reason is communicated (text or aria-label)
No empty, unlabeled container exists that confuses screen reader users
Super Admin cards may show 'All Permissions' or equivalent indication
Screen reader users understand the permissions state for every admin
testCases.postconditions: Absence of tags is communicated clearly

testCases.title: Permission tags are not announced as interactive when they are static
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with permission tags is displayed
steps: Navigate to permission tags using screen reader
Verify tags are NOT announced as buttons, links, or other interactive roles (unless they are clickable)
Verify tags do not receive keyboard focus via Tab (unless interactive)
Verify no misleading ARIA roles are applied
expectedResults: Static permission tags are announced as text content (not buttons or links)
Tags do not appear in the Tab order if they are not interactive
No misleading role='button' or role='link' on static tags
Screen reader users are not confused about whether tags are actionable
testCases.postconditions: Tags correctly represent their non-interactive nature

testCases.title: Permission tags have adequate spacing for readability
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with multiple permission tags is displayed
steps: Apply WCAG text spacing overrides (line-height 1.5x, paragraph spacing 2x, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em)
Verify permission tag text remains readable
Verify tags do not overlap or clip after spacing changes
Verify the layout adapts to increased spacing
expectedResults: Tag text remains readable with increased spacing
No text is clipped or hidden
Tags do not overlap each other
Layout adapts gracefully to spacing overrides
testCases.postconditions: Tags are readable with custom text spacing
